studies.Reference: Relationship between calcium, lactose, vitamin D, and dairy products and ovarian cancer.
studies.Authors: Koralek DO, Bertone-Johnson ER, Leitzmann MF, Sturgeon SR, Lacey JV, Schairer C, Schatzkin A
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: The authors investigated the association between these foods and nutrients and ovarian cancer risk among 31,925 subjects in the Breast Cancer Detection Demonstration Project follow-up cohort.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: 31,925 subjects in the Breast Cancer Detection Demonstration Project follow-up cohort.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: statistically nonsignificant inverse association between high dietary calcium intake and ovarian cancer (RR = 0.67; 95% CI = 0.43, 1.04; P for trend = 0.08).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: statistically nonsignificant inverse association between high dietary calcium intake and ovarian cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Over an average follow-up of 8.3 yr, 146 incident ovarian cancer cases were confirmed.

studies.Reference: Independent and joint effects of serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D and calcium on ovarian cancer risk: a prospective nested case-control study.
studies.Authors: Toriola AT, Surcel HM, Calypse A, Grankvist K, Luostarinen T, Lukanova A, Pukkala E, Lehtinen M
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: We investigated the association between pre-diagnostic serum calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25-OHD) on the risk of later development of ovarian cancer.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: The cohort subset comprised 172 ovarian cancer cases with 172 matched controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Relative risk (estimated as odds ratio, OR) comparing the highest quartile to the lowest quartile was significantly decreased; 0.41.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: We observed a significant inverse association between calcium and ovarian cancer risk.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: We investigated the association between pre-diagnostic serum calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25-OHD) on the risk of later development of ovarian cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: We investigated the association between pre-diagnostic serum calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25-OHD).

studies.Reference: Prediagnostic serum calcium and albumin and ovarian cancer: A nested case-control study in the Norwegian Janus Serum Bank Cohort.
studies.Authors: Schwartz GG, Tretli S, Vos L, Robsahm TE
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Serum calcium was measured from blood samples.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: We compared 202 ovarian cancer cases and 202 controls.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: In early follow-up, women in the highest tertile of serum calcium had a 2.5-fold increased risk, adjusted for height and body mass index (OR=2.47, 95% C.I. 1.12-5.45).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Women in the highest tertile of serum calcium had a 2.5-fold increased risk.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: Women with higher serum calcium may be more likely to be diagnosed with ovarian cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Serum calcium was measured from blood samples.

studies.Reference: Prospective studies of total and ionized serum calcium in relation to incident and fatal ovarian cancer.
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Serum calcium was measured in the NHANES Epidemiological Follow-up Study (NHEFS).

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Eight incident ovarian cancers occurred over 31,089 person-years of follow-up in the NHEFS.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: After adjusting for covariates, there was a 63% higher risk for ovarian cancer with each 0.1 mmol/L increase in total serum calcium.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Higher serum calcium may be a biomarker of ovarian cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: We then examined the associations of serum calcium with incident ovarian cancer in a second prospective cohort, the NHANES Epidemiological Follow-up Study (NHEFS).
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: We examined the associations between total and ionized serum calcium and ovarian cancer.

studies.Reference: Association of dairy products, lactose, and calcium with the risk of ovarian cancer.

studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Consumption of calcium was assessed through dietary intake interviews.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: A total of 558 patients with ovarian cancer diagnosed in 1993-1999 and 607 controls were interviewed regarding their diet.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The odds ratio for ovarian cancer was 0.46 (95% confidence interval: 0.27, 0.76) among women in the highest quartile of dietary calcium intake versus the lowest.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: Consumption of calcium was significantly inversely related to the odds of ovarian cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: The study examined the risk of ovarian cancer incidence.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_definition: Calcium intake was assessed through dietary interviews.

studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: In models that were simultaneously adjusted for total (dietary plus supplements) calcium, total vitamin D and lactose, we observed a decreased overall risk of ovarian cancer with high intake of total calcium.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Using data from the New England case-control study (1,909 cases and 1,989 controls).
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: we observed a decreased overall risk of ovarian cancer with high intake of total calcium.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger's test indicates no significant funnel plot asymmetry (p=0.9235). The distribution of studies appears symmetric, suggesting a lower risk of publication bias.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 8 studies yielded an effect size of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.57–1.07), indicating no statistically significant association between calcium and ovarian cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 82.82%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
